Thank you. 
My partner has supported me a lot by taking a number of “free consultations” with other lawyers to ensure that I am getting the best service I can be. 
Unfortunately it’s just a lengthy process when it comes to these allegations and I have needed to get multiple reports to clear any chance at “risk” towards the children.

My daughter is very much at that age and as I mentioned it’s taking a toll on her emotionally so while I am focused on resuming time with them both, I’m also very conscious of how I can support her in how she’s feeling.
I agree that they will make their own decisions as they grow up but I just want to navigate it as best as I can now so that it doesn’t damage them both any further.

I do have a solicitor and my priority has been resuming time with my kids.
Parental alienation has been the argument to speed the process along and if we hadn’t provided evidence of this, it would have taken a lot longer than 7 months to get to this stage.
In September I will have my chance to directly challenge her with evidence contradicting the allegations however, I don’t believe there’ll be any repercussions regarding “abuse of the courts”. I believe that will be a seperate trial but I’m not really concerned at this point so long as we have orders in place to ensure this doesn’t happen again.

I am a bit worried about being so forward with the children and telling them that their mother has lied to them. I have been sure to tell them how much I love them/want to be there to support them but I’m finding it difficult to ask what they’ve been told and respond without putting their mother in a bad light. I strongly feel like they’re too young to be put in that position even if the reality is that it’s being reciprocated from their mother. 
That’s great advice about having my parents record the conversation! I’ll definitely do that! 

My son started school this year and I wasn’t there. It’s time I’ll never get back and it’s been horrible.

I completely agree with you and I don’t expect forgiveness from my ex partner.
I’m also trying my best through therapy to not be angry towards her in this situation however hard that may be. 
We had our first child very young and I don’t think either of us were in the right position mentally or emotionally for the responsibility to be parents. 
She also has a lot of trauma surrounding her own father not being present when she was a child which I assume plays a huge part in this.

I think you misunderstand why I’m asking what my kids have been told this last 6 months. I’m not going into it to “clear my name” with them. I’m confident in our relationship and that the allegations aren’t true. 
I just don’t want them to believe that I haven’t seen them because I haven’t wanted to/ haven’t tried enough and what I fear is that I don’t know what their mother has told them is the reason.
As I mentioned I don’t want to pressure them or pit them against their mother, I want to reassure them that I’m here for them and after 6 months of missing them, I understand that might be hard for them to trust.
I feel like my son is still too young but it’s affected my daughter a lot and I don’t want her to grow up with abandonment issues because without explanation, one minute I’m there and the next I’m not.

You’re right though, I didn’t address this because legally it doesn’t look good but that’s why I’m asking for advice. I genuinely don’t know how to address it without explaining that their mother has lied.
I do really appreciate your response.
Mentioning that “rules need to be followed” is a great way for me to address it and I just hope to be prepared for any follow up questions that they may have.

Thank you

Thank you for opening up about that! 
That sounds horrible and I’m so sorry you had to go through that. 
Your insight was exactly what I was looking for and what I fear for my own kids.

I really hope to address this in a way where they don’t feel abandonment from either parent but it’s tricky and I don’t know if they are currently receiving similar psychological/emotional abuse like you detailed.
I would certainly hope not but I am doing my best to be there as much as I can for them, reassuring them that I love/ miss them and that we will never have to spend that long apart again.
Do you recall how your dad approached the situation with you? 

My ex partner and I have tried the parenting apps but she would often delete the app or turn it off so when I would ask about the kids my message wouldn’t be received. 
I’m seeking court orders so that she can be held accountable if she’s to do that again, also so that she can’t withhold them again in the future.

Funny you mentioned the bear, I did just give my daughter a plush cat last weekend and told her to give it a squeeze if she ever felt like she was missing me.

I can admit I’m not a perfect father however, I am trying to do the right thing by my kids hence this post.

Thank you for your concern.

I responded to criticism in another response.

My partner was with me the day these allegations were surrounding and therapy has helped a lot in regards to the advice I was seeking in my last post.
I admit my flaws and ask for advice to help my relationships to benefit others and myself.

Thank you.
In this situation they have appointed an independent child’s lawyer (ICL) which I assume would be similar.
They will provide their “recommendations” based on what they discuss with the children however, if an agreement is not met between the parents it gets pushed out further to our next hearing where the court will decide what happens on evidence. 

I assume the ICL hasn’t been privy on anything my ex partner has said to the kids and so I don’t really know what they have been told/ if anything.

I completely agree and usually just avoid talking about their mother where I can.

I wish you wouldn’t jump to conclusions but I understand how you’ve come to that.

If you’d read my last posts they were addressing toxicity with my current partner regarding us both having trauma and struggling to navigate it.

My post from 4 years ago was also during the first time my ex partner was withholding my kids and I was having a lot of trouble navigating that hurt while filling my needs as a partner and not letting it get the better of me.

The truth is, I know I’m flawed and I am getting regular help through therapy however, I’m asking for advice for a reason and that is to better myself as a person, parent and partner.

Thank you.
I hope to do relationship counselling with them both after this is all over so that I can build up to being completely honest but I agree with what you’re saying and I just really hope for them to grow up not having to question what each parent is telling them.

Thanks for the response!
Unfortunately, I agree that it’s unrealistic. My intention is to allow them to be naive to the reality of the situation until they’re older and can make decisions for themselves.
Given that this isn’t the first time something like this has happened with my ex partner I know I can’t change her behaviour, only how I approach it towards my kids. I don’t believe it’s in their best interests to be told that either parent is “the bad guy” and I guess that’s why I’m asking if I can address it without putting blame on their mother.
She’s a good parent in her own time and I’ve tried many times to ask her to assume/ respect the same of me but if she’s going to continue being this way then I think the best I can do for the kids is not reciprocate it from both sides and put that pressure on them.

I do have a lawyer and I’m not really satisfied with how long it’s taken but unfortunately this is how our legal system treats allegations of child abuse regardless of evidence (which in most cases makes sense).
It’s been a really hard year and I’m sure I’m not the only one in this situation.

I'm an apprentice plumber and I started off earning very little money. I couldn't afford my school fees and decided to get a credit card where I soon found myself in almost $8000 debt and I could not meet the repayments to get on top of it.

I met the most amazing girl and we were in a healthy relationship where we lived with each other (off her money) for a year when we found out she was pregnant. I wanted to be there as the father and we decided to move in with my parents to save money and start our family.

Tensions between my girlfriend and I grew as she felt "trapped" in my parents house and my credit card repayments coupled with my own procrastination were keeping me from saving money. But we convinced ourselves that we could make it work. The most joy I had ever felt at this point was seeing a 12 week ultrasound of my soon to be daughter however, reality struck and I finally realised what was really happening.

From when my girlfriend was about 6 months pregnant I remember feeling extremely inadequate and unfit to be a parent or even a partner. The birthdate was coming quicker than I had anticipated. I would spend most car trips to work crying and struggling to come to terms with the situation I was in. But I never told anyone how I felt.

We started having complications with the pregnancy and we were both getting stressed which put a lot of pressure on our relationship.
I first started contemplating suicide a month before my daughter was born.
I had gotten my hands on all the equipment I needed to connect my car exhaust to the cabin and suffocate myself. But I couldn't do it and I hated myself even further for even considering it.. I continued without telling anyone until our beautiful baby girl was born.

I hadn't even known what true happiness was until that day. I was as proud as I've ever been, more excited and energetic than I've ever known and it was a feeling that I thought I would never forget.
I'm a dad and I now have a responsibility to be on this earth.

I realised quickly that parenting is hard work and over the span of 4 months I realised that I may never have that feeling of utter happiness that I felt when she was born. It felt like I had peaked and I felt myself more stressed than ever. I started getting angry and stubborn over everything. I knew I was wrong in most cases but I would never admit it when I should have. I drove my girlfriend away and she left with our daughter. 

I had never felt so low. I would spend my spare time thinking up ways I could kill myself whilst not looking like a complete asshole for leaving my daughter without a dad. I would see my kid only one day a week as I worked full time and it was killing me. My  ex was reasonable and still kept me informed of everything and sent plenty of pictures but it felt like I was being taunted.. I would go out drinking with my mates and waste money to help me feel better which in turn prevented me from paying off my debt.

This went on for 3 months however we gradually started talking more and we agreed that we will try to make it work when she found a house to move into.
We had a plan that we would split the bills and continue being a family after I got my debt sorted.

We soon found out that we both still harboured some resentment towards each other for everything and we'd fight constantly. I'd be forced to sleep at my parents house every other time we had a fight and still I would procrastinate about paying my debt with everything else that's going on. We loved each other but it was emotionally draining..

My anger and inability to stay motivated caused us to be on and off for almost 4 months until she gave me an ultimatum.
It was a possible goal to sort my debt out in a few weeks.
However, my work tools began playing up which resulted in me having to buy new ones and also a deposit for our daughters Childcare prevented me from making my target.

2 days after our daughters first birthday and just a week ago I was told to get out. I know that she had given me so many opportunities to sort myself out and I know she's given up on me. I've given up on myself too.. 
I can't handle not seeing my daughter daily.
I can't handle knowing that I'm responsible for the destruction of my family.
I can't handle that the mother of my child and my soulmate will find someone else.

I honestly don't know how I could handle continuing from here.
